Factions.Name: Moria
Factions.Description: Khazad-dûm is a Dwarven city beneath the Misty Mountains. Its slow, durable infantry and deep infrastructure excel at holding ground, but it lacks mounted troops and can be vulnerable in open terrain.

Technologies.Name: Deep Delving
Technologies.History: The Khazad sink shafts deeper than any other kindred dares, and the deep veins pay them in stone and metal.
Technologies.Description: Workers +15% stone and metal gather rate.

Technologies.Name: Deep Larders
Technologies.History: Salted meats, sealed grain and stone-cool store-vaults preserve food through siege and winter.

Technologies.Name: Deep Roadways
Technologies.History: The long roads under the mountains are graded true, so a Dwarf can keep pace beneath the earth.

Technologies.Name: Dwarven Axe-mastery
Technologies.History: A Khazad axe is laid on the anvil for a year and swung for a moment, and that moment ends the fight.

Technologies.Name: Khazad Forging
Technologies.History: The halls of Khazad-dûm are hewn and braced to stand against everything the deep can send against them.

Technologies.Name: Pacts with Dale
Technologies.History: The Dwarves trade their craft and steel for the grain of Dale and Esgaroth.
Technologies.Description: Traders +15% trade gain, received as food.

Technologies.Name: Stone-halls of the Dwarves
Technologies.History: Dwarven halls rise course by course in a determined shift, for a Khazad works fastest when the stone is hot to shape.

Heroes.Name: Durin VI
Heroes.History: Durin strengthens the health of nearby infantry.

Heroes.Name: Fundin
Heroes.History: Fundin improves nearby stone and metal gathering.

Heroes.Name: Náin
Heroes.History: Náin improves nearby infantry attacks, including their ability to damage structures.

CivBonuses.Name: Mithril Core
CivBonuses.History: Deep beneath Khazad-dûm the Dwarves work veins no other people can reach, drawing metal long after lesser mines run dry.
CivBonuses.Description: Depleted metal sites continue at 50% normal yield while the required deep-mining structure remains active.

CivBonuses.Name: Tunnel Network
CivBonuses.History: The mines of Moria are a maze of halls and shafts known only to the Dwarves, letting them move unseen between fortified gates.
CivBonuses.Description: Linked tunnel entrances grant +7% movement speed; entrances are visible, attackable, and can be blocked or disabled.

CivBonuses.Name: Deep Guard
CivBonuses.History: Few in number and slow to march, the hosts of Moria hold their ground where others break, shield-wall against charge and storm.
CivBonuses.Description: Durable but slow infantry with strong armour; weak in open terrain against cavalry and siege.

Structures.Name: Mithril Deep-Shaft
Structures.History: Moria's miners sink shafts into the deep veins beneath the mountains.
Structures.Description: Trickles metal while standing and accepts metal and stone only; shafts must be spaced apart.

Structures.Name: Tunnel Mouth
Structures.History: The Dwarves know hidden roads through the halls beneath the mountains.
Structures.Description: Links to another Tunnel Mouth to move garrisoned units underground; linked mouths can be attacked and destroyed.

Structures.Name: The Dwarrowdelf
Structures.History: The great halls of Khazad-dûm stand as the last defense of the Dwarrowdelf.
Structures.Description: While the wonder stands, Moria's structures gain +50% health and are much harder to capture.
